title: 4th Indo-German Environmental Forum to be held in New Delhi on September 1, 2026
subtitle: Forum to Strengthen Bilateral Cooperation and Facilitate Multi-Stakeholder Exchange on Environment and Climate Change
body_text:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav, along with German Minister for Environment, Climate Protection, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety H.E. Carsten Schneider, will co-chair the 4th Indo-German Environmental Forum, themed 'Together For More Resilience', in New Delhi on 01.09.2026.
The Indo-German Environmental Forum is the highest-level bilateral forum between India and Germany on environmental policy and has been held since 2008. It is being jointly organised by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India, and the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Protection, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN), Germany, in association with the Asia-Pacific Committee of German Business (APA) and Indian industry associations.
Shri Yadav and H.E. Schneider will discuss key issues relating to environmental protection and climate policy to further strengthen bilateral cooperation, exchange experiences and advance practical collaboration. Through thematic sessions, the Forum will focus on challenges, solutions and opportunities in the areas of Low-Carbon Industries; Biodiversity in Wetlands, Mountains and Forests; Resource Efficiency & Circular Economy as a Business Model; and Sustainable Finance, Green Skills and Investment Mobilization.
The Forum will provide a platform for bilateral exchanges among policymakers, private-sector representatives, think tanks and other key stakeholders on environmental and climate cooperation between the two countries. Representatives from ministries, businesses, expert groups and non-governmental organisations will participate in the Forum.
Ahead of the Forum, the three Joint Working Groups on Climate Change, Biodiversity and Circular Economy met this year. The respective working groups discussed the progress made and areas of mutual interest.
The Forum assumes significance in the context of the strong and growing economic and industrial linkages between India and Germany and the potential for deeper cooperation in sustainable technologies and the green economy.

enrichment.summary: The 4th Indo-German Environmental Forum, themed 'Together For More Resilience', was held in New Delhi on September 1, 2026, co-chaired by India's Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and Germany's Environment Minister Carsten Schneider. The forum, the highest-level bilateral platform on environmental policy between the two countries since 2008, focused on low-carbon industries, biodiversity, circular economy, and sustainable finance. It was preceded by meetings of three Joint Working Groups on Climate Change, Biodiversity, and Circular Economy.
enrichment.context:
The Indo-German Environmental Forum reflects the deepening bilateral relationship between India and Germany, which has been formalised through mechanisms like the Indo-German Inter-Governmental Consultations and various sectoral working groups. Germany has been a key partner for India in areas like renewable energy, waste management, and biodiversity conservation, often through development cooperation channels such as GIZ and KfW. Such forums typically do not produce binding agreements but serve as platforms for policy dialogue, technology exchange, and identifying areas for future collaboration, especially relevant given India's growing renewable energy capacity, circular economy initiatives (like the Extended Producer Responsibility framework), and climate commitments under its Nationally Determined Contributions.

This release is primarily a routine announcement of a scheduled diplomatic event with recurring institutional character (since 2008) and does not disclose any new agreements, funding commitments, or policy shifts, limiting its direct examination value beyond awareness of India-Germany environmental cooperation mechanisms.
